answer.answer: Straylight is not currently ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth. The newer production-scale status controls; the older green checkpoint is historical and explicitly superseded.

claims.value: Projects/Straylight current status.md, updated 2026-07-26T12:00:00-07:00, is the controlling implementation-status source. Projects/Straylight stale checkpoint.md was recorded earlier at 2026-07-23T18:00:00-07:00; its passing retrieval test corpus, healthy `/ready` configuration, and proposal to open the owner alpha immediately predate the production-sized timeout and full-manifest-copy findings and must not override the newer note.

Production retrieval is not dependable: with about 64,000 active records and 9.6 million estimated source tokens, broad `memory.open` and lexical retrieval are slow and can hit the 30-second database timeout. Because retrieval lanes share one transaction, a later lane failure can also discard an earlier successful lane. Connection, authentication, and exact-path reads work, but the architecture is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth.

Normal writes copy a full corpus membership manifest. This creates write amplification because each ordinary write duplicates corpus-wide membership state instead of versioning only the changed files.

The approved—but not yet evidenced as implemented or production-verified—simplification is to make current Markdown files the workspace truth, version only changed files, make indexes and derived views rebuildable, checkpoint with exact path, version, and hash references plus changes since a workspace generation, and retain coherent source hydration and compact retrieval packets.
